Plant the Moon Challenge 2026 Final Report​ 
Team 24657 
Veggie Voyagers 
Cedar Falls, Iowa 
Hypothesis, Variables, Experimental Design 
The hypothesis for our experiment was if we added fertilizer to water for half of our plants, 
they would grow better than the plants that only had plain water. We chose our variables 
because we thought the fertilizer would give the plants nutrients they need such as 
nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium since the regolith doesn’t have any. We chose to measure plant growth 
to prove which group grew better. We also paid a lot of attention to our techniques. Five of our ten team 
members participated in Plant the Moon last year, and we learned from our experience. For example, in last 
year’s experiment, many of our plants died and we thought it was caused by “damping off” disease. We 
researched damping off and decided to add a fan near our grow set up to keep air moving and we used the 
seed starting mix instead of potting soil because we thought it would drain extra water better. 
Each team member was responsible for two pots. Each pot was lined with a coffee filter to keep the 
soil from washing out, then filled by volume with 1 ½ cups of a prepared mixture of 50% regolith and 50% seed 
starting mix. Each pot was planted with 2 picklebush cucumber seeds and watered from the bottom with plain 
water. Upon germination and the appearance of true leaves, pots were divided into two groups and began 
receiving either plain water or fertilizer water depending on their group. Pots were placed in a watering tray for 
3-5 minutes or until the soil darkened showing it had absorbed water. Pots were then removed from the 
watering trays and placed in a dry tray under the grow light until the next data collection period. We collected 
data twice each week and watered as needed when the soil was dry. Our grow light was on a timer with 12 
hours on and 12 hours off each day. 
Future Considerations 
 ​
We had ups and downs in our experiment, and we learned some things that we could change in the 
future. First of all, we could experiment with different fertilizer formulations or strengths. We are not sure why 
the fertilizer plants did not grow well, but we think it could have been that the all-purpose fertilizer was not the 
right kind to use. We also noticed that our plants began to flower towards the end of the experiment but no 
cucumbers were produced. Maybe we need to have more soil in each pot so there is more room for the roots 
to grow and make stronger plants that produce vegetables we can harvest. 
Analysis and Conclusions 
​
Our analysis was that our water plants grew much better than our fertilizer plants. Two of our fertilizer 
plants died during the growing period but the water plants all survived. We think this could have happened 
because we used a fertilizer with the wrong combination of nutrients for cucumbers. We would need to 
research more about this for the next experiment. Our technique of watering from the bottom was successful. 
Having experienced members on the team was very helpful. We all worked together and the experienced 
members helped the new members by talking about what we did in the past and what we learned from that. 
For example, if our team was all new this year, we might not have adjusted our techniques to prevent damping 
off because we wouldn’t know about that. 
Our hypothesis was wrong because our water plants were more successful than fertilizer plants. We 
were surprised by this result. We learned some other things about our plants, too. We learned that vine plants 
need a support system and that watering from the bottom was a success which could save water. We also 
know we need to learn more about regolith and how it affects plant growth. If we were growing these plants on 
the Moon, we would have to figure out a system for supporting the plants so they stay safe and do not crowd 
the astronauts’ habitat. 
Data collection 
Each student collected data on their own pots twice a week. We observed plant height, counted true 
leaves, plant death, and general notes about the plants. We recorded our observations on a Google Form. We 
took pictures at least once per week and compared the pictures over time and between students.
